newsitem.title: SPAIN: Labour reforms boost permanent contracts-Lab Min.
newsitem.headline: Labour reforms boost permanent contracts-Lab Min.

text.p: The Spanish Labour Ministry said on Thursday that labour reforms which took effect May 17 had boosted stability in the labour market and led to an increase in the number of permanent contracts registered in July.
The ministry forecast that permanent contracts would account for 9.4 percent of all contracts in July compared with just 3.2 percent a year earlier.

Meanwhile, the number of temporary contracts are expected to account for 90.5 percent of all contracts in July compared with 96.75 percent in 1996. The total number of labour contracts is forecast to rise to 976,000 compared with 839,530.

In May, the government introduced labour reforms agreed between unions and employers, aimed at improving stability in the labour market, reducing the cost of dismissals and easing Spain's unemployment.
Of the 92,000 permanent contracts expected to be registered in July, around 70,000 correspond to the regulations set out in the labour reforms, the ministry said.
In the period May 17 to the end of July, the ministry estimates that some 125,000 permanent contracts were registered under the orbit of the new regulations.
More than 70 percent of permanent contracts formed under the new legislation were conversions from temporary contracts.
